'''Bodil Holst''' is a Danish-Norwegian physicist known for her work on [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] imaging, 2D material characterisation and mask based lithography using [[molecular beam]]s.{{r|scino|trinity|prl2018|pra2019|nanolace}} Other research areas include smart surfaces {{r|nano2018|carbon2019}} and plant fibre identification. {{r|science2010|youtube2015}} She is CEO of the company [https://lacelithography.com/ Lace Lithography] and affiliated professor in the Department of Physics and Technology at the [[University of Bergen]] in Norway.{{r|uib}} 

==Education and career==
Holst studied physics and mathematics at the [[University of Copenhagen]]. In 1997, she earned a doctorate at the [[University of Cambridge]]. {{r|mohn}} She continued as a postdoctoral researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Fluid Dynamics in Göttingen, Germany and at the [[Graz University of Technology]] in Austria. On the verge of giving up her academic career, she came to the [[University of Bergen]] in 2007, funded by a recruitment grant from the Trond Mohn Foundation.{{r|scino}} Since 2023 she is CEO of the company  Lace Lithography, which she founded together with her former PhD student Adria Salvador Palau. 

==Books==
Bodil Holst is the author of the self-published book ''Scientific Paper Writing: A Survival Guide'' (2015), illustrated by [[Jorge Cham]].{{r|chemworld}} With Gianangelo Bracco, she is the co-editor of the book ''Surface Science Techniques'' (Springer, 2013).

==Recognition==
2025 Awarded The Research Council of Norway's Innovation Award<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=Bodil Holst vinner Forskningsrådets innovasjonspris |url=https://www.forskningsradet.no/nyheter/2025/bodil-holst-vinner-forskningsradets-innovasjonspris/}}</ref> <br>
2023 Elected to the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] <br> 
2019 Appointed Chair of the [[Kavli Prize]] Committee in Nanoscience for the period 2019-2024. {{r|KavliPrize}}<br> 
2018 Elected to the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]] <br>
2015 Elected to the [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]]<br>
2008 Elected to the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] Commission on Symbols, Units, Nomenclature, Atomic Masses and Fundamental Constants for the period 2008–2011 and re-elected in 2011 for the period 2011-2014<ref>{{Cite web |last=iupap |date=2021-03-31 |title=Archive Commission Members - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/commissions/archive-commission-members/ |access-date=2025-01-16 |language=en-US}}</ref><br>
2007 Trond Mohn Research Foundation Recruitment Grant<br>
2000 [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] Fellowship<br>
1999 [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions]] Research Fellowship
